original_question: Given a graph together with its eigenvalues and eigenspaces, provide necessary and sufficient conditions for instantaneous uniform mixing to occur, where instantaneous uniform mixing means that at some time t all entries of U(t) have the same absolute value, equivalently all entries of the mixing matrix M(t) = U(t) o U(-t) are equal.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open Problem 3.3: “Given the eigenvalues and eigenspaces of a graph, give necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform mixing to occur.” This is the general spectral-characterization problem posed after the time-dependent association-scheme criterion in Corollary 3.3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target very closely: it asks for a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of instantaneous uniform mixing from the graph’s eigenvalues and eigenspaces, and it uses the same equivalent definition of uniform mixing via either equal absolute values of the entries of U(t) or equal entries of the mixing matrix M(t). That is exactly the direction of Open Problem 3.3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
missing_details: State the continuous-time quantum-walk setup explicitly: G is a finite graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A, and U(t)=exp(itA) for real t. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

Specify the spectral data in the paper’s notation as a full spectral decomposition A=∑_{r=0}^d θ_r E_r, where the E_r are the orthogonal idempotents/projections onto the eigenspaces. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
Make the existential quantifier explicit: the question is to determine when there exists a real time τ at which uniform mixing occurs. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

Clarify that the desired characterization should be expressed purely in terms of the eigenvalues and eigenspaces themselves, not by assuming extra structure such as being a cycle, circulant, distance-regular graph, or relation of an association scheme. Open Problem 3.3 is general, while Corollary 3.3 is only for the association-scheme setting. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

Include the nearby motivation that the sought characterization is meant to avoid dependence on a pre-specified mixing time, since the paper identifies time-dependence as the main drawback of Corollary 3.3. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))

If you keep the mixing-matrix phrasing, define M(t)=U(t)◦U(-t) and note that the paper states the equivalence between “all entries of M(τ) are equal” and “all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value.” ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
refined_question: Let G be a finite graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A and spectral decomposition A=∑_{r=0}^d θ_r E_r. For the continuous-time quantum walk U(t)=e^{itA}, determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed solely in terms of the spectral data {(θ_r,E_r)}_{r=0}^d, for the existence of a real time τ such that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing; that is, such that all entries of U(τ) have the same absolute value. The characterization should depend only on the eigenvalues and eigenspaces, rather than on a time-dependent criterion tailored to a particular τ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent formulation used explicitly in Section 3: characterize, from the eigenvalues and eigenspaces of G, exactly when there exists a real time τ such that every entry of the mixing matrix M(τ)=U(τ)◦U(-τ) is equal. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
justification: The draft is not primarily aiming at Open Problem 3.1 (roots of unity for eigenvalues of U(τ)) or at the association-scheme criterion in Corollary 3.3. Instead, it asks for a general necessary-and-sufficient condition for uniform mixing from spectral data, which is precisely Open Problem 3.3. The surrounding context matters: Section 3 defines U(t), M(t), and uniform mixing; Corollary 3.3 gives a necessary-and-sufficient test only in the association-scheme case and still depends on the time t; the authors then say that this time-dependence is a major drawback and pose Open Problem 3.3 as the broader spectral characterization problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.02236))
